assumptions.what: Prop starts its flow at zero, F(0) = 0.
assumptions.sensitivity: Starting at the prior Y changes the scores by a median 8e-5 (relative, up to 7%) and matches none of 17,406 tested pairs; F(0) = 0 matches all to 5e-12.

assumptions.what: OPHID's RW and Prop scores use a self-interaction on every protein (HPRD's use only HPRD's own 1,839).
assumptions.sensitivity: Without them OPHID RW scores differ by a median 14% (131 of 208,509 equal); with them all 208,509 are equal.

assumptions.what: MCL is the micans.org program, release 14-137, inflation 2.0 (the supplement's value); the authors' release is not stated.
assumptions.sensitivity: Its clusters give all 386,070 MCL scores of both networks exactly.

items.label: Python package diseasenet and its tutorial

page.lede: Navlakha and Kingsford released their predictions but not their code. We rebuilt the methods from the paper, reran them on the same networks, and compared every number the paper prints or draws. {exact} of {attempted} attempted results came back exactly, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly agree and {differs} differ; {not_attempted} were not attempted.
page.items_caption: Every figure, table and number of the paper, with the verdict check_results.py computes from our run. Figure values are read from the vector drawings in the paper's PDF.
page.claims_line: The main findings of the paper hold: random walks are the most precise single methods, the consensus is Pareto optimal, and homophilic diseases are predicted better. Three Sec. 3.1 ranges and four Supp. Table 1 scores are slips in the paper; the consensus points differ because the forest's settings are not stated.
came_back: Neighborhood, Oti, RW and Prop rebuilt from the text, and MCL 14-137, give the authors' scores on all 1,935,350 candidate pairs of HPRD and OPHID.
Every point the paper draws for the 13 single methods, on both networks.
Every margin, bar, error bar, count and legend value.
Every count and percentage, and the same named diseases.
diseasenet, a Python package of the methods with a tutorial.
buried: The graph summarization code (GS1-3, GS-All) and the tree VI-Cut cuts: their scores come only from the authors' files.
The consensus forest's settings: our five points are near the paper's, not on them.
Which grid made three points vanish from Fig. 2a.
page.matched_intro: Some settings are not in the paper. We found them by matching the authors' own prediction files and figures, and list them so that a reader can judge.
matched: 0.05 steps for fractions; 0.0001-0.09 for RW; 0.01-0.9 for Prop.
Every protein has a self-interaction in the walks.
Neighbours counted among annotated genes only.
Only method-disease pairs with a prediction; error bars are variances.
page.closing: Dug up on 11 November 2026 from the paper's 2010 web site, as the Wayback Machine kept it.
